newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds slip but outperform Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds slip but outperform Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond prices slipped but outperformed waning U.S. Treasury prices with help from strong followthrough bidding for fresh new issuance, dealers said.
"The market hasn't lost anything with the supply coming in," said one high-grades trader. "Remember there hasn't been much issuance on the whole, too."
Reflecting the demand, NationsBank's $1.4 billion, three-part deal traded higher in all tranches on Thursday, trader said.

NationsBank's 20-year notes, priced to yield 80 basis points over Treasuries, were quoted at 78 bid, 77 offer at the close; the 10-year notes, priced at 68 basis points over, were quoted at 66 bid, 65 offer; and the five-year notes, priced at 43 basis points over, were quoted at 43 bid, 41 offer.

High-grade investors also soaked up Philip Morris' $650 million five-year note deal priced on Thursday, traders said. The deal, increased in size by $150 million, was priced to yield 67 basis points over Treasuries.
One trader termed the spread generous.

Corporate spreads in most sectors were little changed or firmer in thin trade, prices outperforming U.S. Treasuries after a combination of strong economic data, dealers said. The market first dipped after the Commerce Department said August housing starts rose 4.5 percent to a 1.525 million annual rate, the highest level since March of 1994.
A drop in jobless claims and a boost in the prices paid index of the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's September survey also fostered the negative sentiment, traders said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 12/32 at 96-10/32 to yield 7.05 percent.
Turning to the junk bond market, prices were scattered lower from 1/8 to 1/4 point in the broad market, traders said, with the exception of some widely-sought new issue paper.

Speedy Muffler's 10.875 percent 10-year issue, priced at par on Wednesday, was quoted at 101-3/4 bid, 102-1/4 offered. Euromax's 11.25 percent debt, priced at par late Tuesday, was quoted at 101-1/4 bid, 101-5/8 offered.
Other aftermarket activity focused on some select junk names including Flagstar and Trump, traders said.
